subject: Remaining fixes and cleanup from feature/in-memory-db
body:
We were unable to finish these before open-sourcing.

Fixes:

- Update payload statuses of finalized blocks in Store::set_block_ancestor_payload_statuses.

- Restrict Store::latest_archivable_index to valid blocks to prevent blocks from getting lost when archiving.

  Rely on the fix in Store::set_block_ancestor_payload_statuses to make binary search possible.

  The contents of Context.payload_statuses no longer have to be submitted before Context.extra_blocks.
  Snapshot tests pass either way, though some behavior is different behind the scenes.
  Submitting payload statuses afterwards prevents archiving, making all blocks remain in memory.

- Revert unnecessary changes in grandine-snapshot-tests and http_api::context.

  Mainnet blocks do not have to be treated as valid.
  It made sense, but it was a workaround to prevent archived blocks from being lost.
  The bug in Store that caused that is now fixed.

- Limit the Storage case of Controller::preprocessed_state_post_block to max_empty_slots.

- Make in-memory mode apply to all databases.
  Some databases were always persistent due to a mistake during the rewrite to the enum-based design.
  There were 2 in runtime::run_after_genesis and 1 in grandine::Context::run.

Cleanup:

- Remove justified block check from Store::unload_old_states.

  Document why it's neither necessary nor sufficient.

- Simplify and finish documenting test does_not_unload_states_that_may_become_anchors.

  Block 4 was unnecessary.
  The last block (previously block 6, now block 4) triggers unloading too.
  It must be at the start of an epoch because unloading is only done when the head is in that position.

  Block 2 was also unnecessary.
  The next block (previously block 3, now block 2) must be in epoch 2 or later to make its attestations count.
  This is not an obstacle in a real network.

  If block 2 is removed, block 1 can be moved into epoch 2 as well.
  No slots have to be empty in that case.

- Move PayloadStatus from fork_choice_store::misc to types::nonstandard.

  The change was already made but reverted when feature/deneb3 was merged into integration.

- Rename StoreConfig::minimal to aggressive and document it.

  The new name is unambiguous and fits better.
  StoreConfig::aggressive sets only one field to a non-default value and the value is not truly minimal.

- Abandon idea to poison WaitGroup and revert partial implementation of it.

  Tests in fork_choice_control that make the mutator panic sometimes hang.
  The hanging makes it hard to tell if the tests failed and necessitates killing them manually.
  The poisoning was intended to make them reliably panic instead of hanging.

  Reimplementing WaitGroup to poison the mutex inside seemed to work at first, but it's still unreliable.

- Remove pointless calls to Store::is_slot_finalized.

- Remove Snapshot::state_before_or_at_slot.

  It was only called by the Controller method of the same name.

- Replace Bytes in database with Arc<[u8]> and document why.

- Use Connection::pragma_update for remaining pragmas.

Documentation improvements:

- Move comment about nomenclature to the root of fork_choice_store and define unloading in it.

  A glossary does not belong near Store::archive_finalized.
  That may have been the right place when the only distinction was between pruning and archiving.
  The doc comment for the crate is a better place for it.

- Document SQLite's treatment of invalid values more accurately.

subject: Block processor & new state cache.
body:
Block processor - performs state transitions and caches the resulting beacon state and block rewards stats.
This is needed to remove unnecessary state transitions during the block production.

State cache - granularly lockable cache with lock acquire timeout.
Granular caching is achieved by having a cache with a global lock and nested mutexes wrapped in Arcs,
and by locking whole cache for tiny amounts of time - only to insert new or clone references of the nested mutexes.

Derived type-level variables can now be expressed without corresponding associated types in Preset.

See https://blog.rust-lang.org/2024/06/13/Rust-1.79.0.html#bounds-in-associated-type-position.

The sugared version of ArrayLengthCopy actually made rustc panic.
We found no reports of similar panics in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues.
Inlining the Copy bound works and is an overall improvement.
ArrayLengthCopy only existed because the Copy bound could not be specified inline.

Copy impls for ContiguousVector and ByteVector are now written manually.
Deriving them with derivative caused multiple issues.
Writing them manually turned out to be no more verbose than deriving them.

subject: Fix 2 bugs in Electra deposit processing
body:
All those fields recently added to CombinedDeposit still weren't enough.

There seems to have been a similar unobserved bug involving PendingDeposit.withdrawal_credentials.
A top-up deposit may contain withdrawal credentials different from the original ones.

apply_deposits in Electra now works around some of the logic in validate_deposits.
validate_deposits does 2 things:
- It verifies signatures in an optimized way.
- It combines deposits with the same pubkey to minimize BeaconState updates.
The former is still useful in Electra, but the latter is undesirable.
It may be a good idea to refactor validate_deposits to only do the former.

subject: Optimize hexadecimal conversions in serde_utils to speed up JSON serialization of byte collections
body:
Slow serialization to JSON was claimed to be the problem that led to 2e92e00246890ae37322c9df05a3cd344e50a57e.
BlobSidecar serialization is now around 15.4 times faster.
BlobSidecar deserialization is now around 12 times faster.
SignedBeaconBlock serialization is now up to 1.5 times faster.
SignedBeaconBlock deserialization is now up to 1.1 times faster.

faster-hex might be faster than const-hex in some cases, but faster-hex does not provide the API we require.
See https://crates.io/crates/const-hex/1.14.0 for benchmark results comparing various hexadecimal conversion crates.

compressed size.

author: Delene Tchio Romuald
subject: fix: use deposit_requests_start_index in Gloas process_operations
body:
The Gloas deposit count validation at gloas/block_processing.rs
uses the pre-Electra formula (deposit_count - eth1_deposit_index) which
ignores deposit_requests_start_index.

The Electra implementation (electra/block_processing.rs:499-524) correctly
uses deposit_requests_start_index to disable the former deposit mechanism
once all prior deposits are processed, per the consensus spec
(gloas/beacon-chain.md line 1157-1158). The Gloas version should use the
same formula.

Without this fix, Grandine would compute a wrong expected deposit count
for Gloas blocks, causing a consensus split.

This commit fixes memory leak in C bindings, where rust container
CVec<T> erronously only deallocated pointer to memory region, containing
list of items, but each of items were not dropped individually. This
caused a memory leak in cases, where CVec<T> container holded items,
requiring additional cleanup - like CExecutionPayloadV{1,2,3}
transactions field, which has type CVec<CTransaction>, where
CTransaction is a wrapper over CVec<u8>.

author: Artiom Tretjakovas
subject: Proper cleanup for method arguments in C bindings
body:
This commit fixes memory leaks in nethermind plugin. The leak was caused
by moving structs, that contain heap allocations, through FFI boundary.
The `Drop` implementations on structs are correct, but rust was
considering those structs "moved" through FFI boundary, thus not calling
`drop`.

This was fixed with passing values by references - after all, receiver
of those objects has to copy them into their own managed memory, so this
gives better semantics.

author: Artiom Tretjakovas
subject: Implement structurally shared validator list
body:
This commit employs Structure of Arrays (SoA) pattern for implementing
validator list container. The validator fields are split into three
lists - pubkeys, effective balances, and rest of fields. Because pubkey
list is strictly append-only, such validator list structure saves memory
when loading historical state from disk - instead of copying every
public key from finalized state into a newly loaded one, we can attach
whole pubkey list at once, re-using memory for all keys.

author: Artiom Tretjakovas
subject: Fix nethermind plugin clean build
body:
Previuosly, when trying to build nethermind plugin through makefile with
`-B` flag, the build was failing with obscure error:

```
    EXEC : warning openssl-sys@0.9.114: building OpenSSL dependencies:
    'make' reported failure with exit status: 2
    EXEC : warning openssl-sys@0.9.114: openssl-src: failed to build
    OpenSSL from source
    EXEC : error failed to run custom build command for
    `openssl-sys v0.9.114`
```

The issue was with `openssl-src` build process. OpenSSL uses make too,
but they require to run the command twice - the second time, caches used
from first run are used, making build pass only from the second run.
However, passing `-B` flag when building `nethermind-plugin` target
propagated flag to openssl, thus caches were cleared during second run,
and openssl build failed.

This patch makes one change - resets `MAKEFLAGS` environment variable,
when generating rust bindings. Although this probably may cause problems
in the future, when someone decides to pass `MAKEFLAGS` environment
variable for their needs (perhaps, doing custom configuration of
downstream dependencies?), this flag will be erased. The solution would
be either to process `MAKEFLAGS` and only remove `-B` flag, to set flags
in `bindings/csharp/build.rs`, or even to contribute into `openssl-src`
rust crate, and adapt their `MAKEFLAGS` environment variable processing.
Nevertheless, currently no such issue exists, so this possible problem
solution is postponed until it actually appears.

subject: Validate bid gas limit against the payload at bid.parent_block_hash
body:
validate_execution_payload_bid derived parent_gas_limit from the parent
block's post-state latest_execution_payload_bid, i.e. the parent block's own
bid, regardless of which payload the bid builds on. The spec keys
parent_gas_limit on bid.parent_block_hash: a bid that builds on the parent's
parent payload (parent payload withheld) must be checked against that
payload's gas limit, which differs from the parent bid's gas limit whenever
the gas limit is moving. Such bids were dropped with "bid gas_limit is not
compatible with target_gas_limit" on gossip and via the publish REST
endpoint (200 + Ignore, never broadcast).

Resolve the chain link carrying the payload identified by
bid.parent_block_hash (the existing execution_payload_locations index) and
use the gas limit committed by that block: its bid post-Gloas, the payload
itself pre-Gloas. Adds ExecutionPayload::gas_limit for the latter.

subject: Fix pubkey recovery for unfinalized states
body:
When unfinalized states are persisted, their keys are zeroized in the
same way as keys in finalized states. However, restoring public keys for
unfinalized states requires more care: only zeroized keys should be
restored, rather than replacing all keys.

This fixes two bugs:

  - unfinalized states with more validators than the latest finalized
    state failed to load because pubkey recovery crashed when the
    finalized state's key list was too short;
  - unfinalized states with the same number of public keys as the

author: Artiom Tretjakovas
subject: Cache shufflings obtained during PTC computation
body:
Previously, the shuffling computed during PTC processing was discarded
and computed again later. It can be reused: the PTC is computed for
current_epoch + 2, and right after that the epoch transition advances
the current epoch, so the same shuffling can be stored as the one for
the next epoch.

The cache cannot simply be extended with a `SecondNext` slot, because
such a shuffling is not correct in general. Its seed depends on the
RANDAO mix of the current epoch, which changes with every block, so it
is only valid at the end of the epoch, which is when the PTC is
computed.

author: Artiom Tretjakovas
subject: Optimize epoch processing for gloas
body:
Currently processing gloas epoch takes ~6.6 seconds. This is due to the
bug, where process_ptc_window computed the PTC for each of the 32 slots,
and each ptc computation was re-doing all the work, including heavy
operations like shuffling. Sharing work accross those ptc computations
lowered epoch processing time down to ~800 ms. Changing `.validators()
.get(i)` with `.validators().effective_balance(i)` in
compute_balance_weighted_selection helper reduced epoch processing time
further, down to ~660ms.

author: Tumas
subject: Run the validator client against remote beacon nodes with the new vc and bn commands
body:
`grandine vc --beacon-node-urls ...` runs the validator client alone
against remote beacon nodes, `grandine bn` runs the beacon node alone,
and the bare command runs the beacon node with the local validator when
one is configured. Duties come from exactly one source: the built-in
node or the remote nodes. vc refuses options that only the built-in
beacon node acts on.

The validator no longer holds the fork choice controller. It works
through a ChainSource, and every duty goes through the BeaconNodeApi
trait, which the built-in node and the remote nodes both implement:
attester, aggregation, sync committee, PTC, proposer, payload
attestation, voluntary exit and doppelganger liveness duties, plus
prepared proposers, validator registrations and proposer preferences.
Attestation data returned by a remote node is validated for the
reported index and target epoch before it is signed. Proposer
preferences are published for the dependent root the duties are held
under.

Remote nodes are polled for health and ranked by it, then by the newest
head; an unreachable node is kept as the last choice. Requests have
per-endpoint timeouts, a head stream tracks reorgs, and a slot head
fallback covers a node that falls behind. Duties are published to every
node by default, returning once one accepts; the payload envelope goes
to the node that produced the block. In remote mode the validator is
driven by clock ticks directly, and genesis is agreed with the nodes
before it starts.

Signing no longer needs a beacon state: the signer takes the fork
information and the current epoch, and slashing protection takes the
epoch. Own validator indices are resolved from the finalized state,
driven by finalization events and by changes to the signer's keys. The
chain is identified by its genesis validators root without loading the
state; vc and the interchange commands use the predefined network's
root, read from the embedded mainnet state or a constant for the
testnets.

Doppelganger protection no longer reads the local beacon state or the
liveness tracker directly: it takes validator indices and a liveness
query from the caller, so it works against remote beacon nodes, where
only synced nodes are asked and a validator seen live by any of them
counts as live. The check runs late in the slot, at the aggregate tick,
when every node has ticked into the epoch and seen the slot's
attestations. A key is activated only after a successful check, a failed
query postpones activation instead of panicking, and a key whose index
is unknown is not activated until its index resolves and a full check
window has passed from that point. A key removed during its check window
starts a new one when it returns. A detected doppelganger stops the
application through a typed error rather than a panic, so it is not
restarted. --detect-doppelgangers needs --track-liveness only with the
built-in beacon node. Sync committee messages no longer count towards
validator liveness.

Register the validator client with the beacon nodes' builder via
--use-builder pre-Gloas, skipping validators without a fee recipient.

Also:
- Leave the peer counts out of validator client logs
- Run data column recovery on its own executor
- Accept a slot's worth of aggregates in one publish request
- Keep peers on subscribed sync committee subnets until the subscription
  expires
- Serve next epoch attester duties from the state at the current slot
  when the head lags, and accept next epoch duty requests sent as the
  clock enters a new epoch
- Let the builder publish a blinded block from Fulu on instead of
  unblinding it
- Reject and don't publish single attestations from validators outside
  the named committee
- Limit concurrent Web3Signer requests for whole-epoch batches
- Send the block event only after fork choice exposes the block's head
- Keep finalized blocks in the store until they are written to storage
- Fix the network dashboard
